ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a single-phase full-bridge inverter, the DC side is labeled 325 V, and the load is connected between points a and b; the Vab waveform on the right is a symmetric quasi-square wave. In the positive half-cycle, Vab is 0 for an initial segment, starts becoming +325 V from angle θ, and remains at a high level in the interval centered at π/2, then returns to 0 before π; in the negative half-cycle, a -325 V pulse appears according to half-wave symmetry. Reasoning: Taking the nonzero interval of the positive half-cycle as θ to π−θ according to the figure, and using half-wave symmetry, it is only necessary to calculate the contribution of the positive half-cycle to the fundamental sine coefficient. b1 = (2/π)∫0^π Vab(x)sin(x)dx = (2/π)∫θ^(π−θ) Vdc sin(x)dx = (2/π)Vdc[-cos(x)]θ^(π−θ) = (4Vdc/π)cosθ. The modulation index is defined as the ratio of the fundamental peak value to the DC voltage, so m = b1/Vdc = (4/π)cosθ. Let m = 0.8, obtaining cosθ = 0.8π/4, θ = cos^(-1)(0.8π/4) = 51.07°, approximately 51.1°.

claims.claim: Using half-wave symmetry, it is only necessary to calculate the contribution of the positive half-cycle to the fundamental sine coefficient.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Using half-wave symmetry, it is only necessary to calculate the contribution of the positive half-cycle to the fundamental sine coefficient

claims.claim: Under the condition of half-wave symmetry, the fundamental sine coefficient can be written as b1 = (2/π)∫0^π Vab(x)sin(x)dx.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: b1 = (2/π)∫0^π Vab(x)sin(x)dx

claims.claim: For this waveform, b1 = (2/π)∫θ^(π−θ) Vdc sin(x)dx.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: = (2/π)∫θ^(π−θ) Vdc sin(x)dx

claims.claim: The integral calculation gives b1 = (2/π)Vdc[-cos(x)]θ^(π−θ).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: = (2/π)Vdc[-cos(x)]θ^(π−θ)

claims.claim: The integral result simplifies to b1 = (4Vdc/π)cosθ.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: = (4Vdc/π)cosθ

claims.claim: The modulation index is defined as the ratio of the fundamental wave peak value to the DC voltage.
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: In this problem, the modulation index m = b1/Vdc.

claims.source: So m = b1/Vdc

claims.claim: In this problem, m = (4/π)cosθ.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: = (4/π)cosθ

claims.claim: Let m = 0.8.

claims.claim: From m = 0.8, obtain cosθ = 0.8π/4.
